transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been feeling a bit too aware of a scar on my wrist. I know it probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep thinking people are looking right at it, like it’s the first thing they see.
How much distress does thinking about the scar cause you?

It bothers me… more than I’d like to admit. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice now.
Has thinking about the scar caused you to avoid any social situations or activities that you would normally enjoy?

A little, yes. I’ve… skipped a few choir things, and some theater volunteer work, because I get too caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t show. And I’ve been late with some bookkeeping work too, which isn’t really like me.
Do you often find yourself thinking about how your body looks to others, beyond just this scar?

Mostly it’s the scar. I mean… I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just feel like everyone’s eyes go right to it. Like that’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Is your concern about the scar mostly about how it looks, or is it about what it might mean to others, like a sign of something about you?

Mostly how it looks, I think. I know it may not be as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just keep thinking people’s eyes go right to my wrist… like that’s what they see first.
Do you worry about how other parts of your body look, or is it mainly just the scar on your wrist that bothers you?
It’s mainly the scar. I don’t really… worry about other parts much. I just keep thinking people notice my wrist first, even though I know it probably isn’t as bad as it feels to me.
Do you think your perception of how noticeable the scar is matches how it actually looks to others?

Probably not, no. I mean… I know it’s likely not as noticeable as it feels to me. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I still feel like people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they see.
Do you find it hard to stop thinking about the scar when you want to?
Yes… sometimes. I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me, but when I’m around people—like at church or bridge—I keep thinking they’re looking right at my wrist. It’s hard to shake.
Have you ever been as concerned about how another part of your body looks as you are about this scar?

No… not really. It’s been the scar, mostly. I know it probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist. Like that’s the first thing they notice now.
Has your concern about the scar ever shifted to another part of your body, even if only for a little while?
No… I don’t think so. It’s really been the scar on my wrist. I know it probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just feel like people notice it right away.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your thoughts about the scar?

Yes… I suppose it feels that way sometimes. I know the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just keep thinking people’s eyes go right to it… like that’s the first thing they notice.
Has thinking about the scar affected your ability to concentrate on work or other tasks you need to do at home?

Yes… a little. I’ve been late getting some bookkeeping things turned in because I get stuck checking whether my wrist is covered. And I’ve skipped a few choir and theater volunteer things, too… just because I didn’t want people noticing it.
Has your worry about the scar affected your relationships with family or friends?

A little, I guess… not directly with family so much. I’ve missed some choir and theater volunteer things, and I’ve been late with bookkeeping work because I get caught up making sure my wrist is covered. So… I suppose it has, in that way.
Does thinking about the scar happen to you every day?
Most days, yes. I try not to dwell on it, but when I’m around people—at church, or bridge—I start feeling like they’re looking right at my wrist. Like it’s the first thing they notice.
Do thoughts about the scar pop into your mind when you're not trying to think about it?
Yes… sometimes. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but it’ll just come into my head, especially before church or bridge. I start thinking people’s eyes go right to my wrist.
Would you say that thinking about the scar is one of the most distressing things you deal with on a daily basis?

Yes… I’d say it’s up there. I know the scar probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep thinking everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist. Like that’s what they notice first now.
Do you think people would think less of you if they noticed the scar?

Maybe… I don’t know if “less of me” exactly. I just feel like if they see it, that’s what they’ll notice first. At church or bridge, I get this feeling their eyes go right to my wrist, even though I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me.
Do you worry that people will judge you or think you're flawed in some way if they see the scar?
A little, yes. I mean… I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me. But when I’m at church or bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like that’s the first thing they see now.
Do you think people would see the scar and think there's something wrong with you as a person?

I don’t know if they’d think there’s something wrong with me as a person… it’s more that I feel like they’d see the scar first. Like at church or bridge, I keep thinking their eyes go right to my wrist, even though I know it’s probably not as bad as it feels to me.
